fullPassage:
What does it mean to be brave? There is no single definition, but everyone is brave in their own way. Here are three young people sharing their bravest moments in life.

Jason: One evening, I went to a convenience store to buy some snacks. No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was working in the back. The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor. I immediately called 911 and explained the situation. The operator asked me to perform CPR on the clerk until the paramedics arrived. I was scared, but I remembered learning CPR at school. I started to push down on his chest, hoping that I was doing it right. A few minutes later, the paramedics rushed in and took over the situation. Luckily, the clerk regained consciousness. After putting the clerk in the ambulance, the paramedics said "Thank you for being brave. You did a wonderful job." It felt great to help save someone's life!

Olivia: I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field athlete. My room was full of medals and awards from races I had competed in. During the national 100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic dreams came to a sudden end. I was about to take the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried off the track. At first, I didn't think much of the injury. I thought I would get better soon. But the test results from the hospital were not hopeful. The doctors said my knee injury would prevent me from running again. Every night, I had flashbacks of my injury. I could not watch sports anymore because it was just too painful. So I shut out everything related to sports from my life. Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my ordinary high school life without sports. Then one day, I came across an interesting university major called sports medicine. It deals with the treatment and prevention of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head. This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears. So I made up my mind and applied to this major. Today, thanks to my brave decision, I am studying to be a star on the sidelines instead of on the playing field.

Yuna: Ever since I was young, I have admired great public speakers. I hoped to inspire and move audiences like them someday. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would get scared. I didn't want to make a fool of myself. This fear kept me behind the stage rather than on it. That's why I never entered the annual speech contest at my school. I really wanted to, but I just didn't have enough courage. Last year, however, was my final chance before graduating from high school. When I saw the poster on the class board, my mind began to fill with thoughts of the school speech contest. I heard a voice growing louder in my head, saying "Go for it!" I decided to sign up for the contest. To make a long story short, I did it. I delivered my speech to the entire school. How did I do? Honestly, I don't remember much from the contest because I was so nervous. But my act of courage taught me a valuable lesson: I can do anything that I put my mind to.

questions.passage: One evening, I went to a convenience store to buy some snacks. No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was working in the back. The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor. I immediately called 911 and explained the situation.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Jason은 점원이 바닥에 서 있는 것을 보았다.
Jason은 이상함을 느끼고 카운터 너머를 살펴보았다.

det.korean: Jason은 뭔가 잘못되었다고 느끼고 카운터 너머를 살펴보았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 원문 일치: I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter
❌ ① Jason은 손님이지 직원이 아님
❌ ② no one came to answer it — 아무도 전화를 받지 않았음
❌ ③ lying on the floor — 바닥에 '누워' 있었지 '서' 있지 않았음
det.tip: lying(누워있는) ≠ standing(서있는). 점원은 바닥에 쓰러져 있었다.

questions.passage: I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field athlete. My room was full of medals and awards from races I had competed in. During the national 100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic dreams came to a sudden end. I was about to take the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in my knee.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문은 medals and awards(메달과 상)이지 트로피가 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 'trophies(트로피)'가 아닌 'medals and awards(메달과 상)' — 내용 불일치
❌ ① 원문 일치: dreamed of being an Olympic track and field athlete
❌ ③ 원문 일치: During the national 100-meter championship race
❌ ④ 원문 일치: suddenly felt a pain in my knee
det.tip: medals and awards(메달과 상) ≠ trophies(트로피). 세부 사항을 정확히 읽어야 한다.

questions.passage: Ever since I was young, I have admired great public speakers. I hoped to inspire and move audiences like them someday. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would get scared. I didn't want to make a fool of myself. This fear kept me behind the stage rather than on it. That's why I never entered the annual speech contest at my school.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F인 것은?
ch: T — Yuna는 어릴 때부터 대중 연설가를 존경했다.
T — Yuna는 사람들 앞에서 말할 때 겁이 났다.
T — Yuna는 매년 학교 연설대회에 참가했다.
F — 두려움이 Yuna를 무대 위가 아닌 뒤에 있게 했다.

det.korean: ③ Yuna는 매년 연설대회에 참가한 적이 없다(never entered).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ T라고 표기되어 있지만 FALSE. never entered — 한 번도 참가하지 않았음
❌ ① T: 올바른 표기, 원문 일치
❌ ② T: 올바른 표기, 원문 일치
❌ ④ F: 올바른 표기. '무대 위가 아닌 뒤에' = behind the stage rather than on it
det.tip: never entered = 한 번도 참가하지 않았다. T/F 판단 시 never, always 같은 빈도 부사에 주의.

questions.passage: The operator asked me to perform CPR on the clerk until the paramedics arrived. I was scared, but I remembered learning CPR at school. I started to push down on his chest, hoping that I was doing it __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 올바르게(right) 하고 있기를 바라면서 가슴을 눌렀다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① right: 원문 일치 — hoping that I was doing it right
❌ ② wrong: 맥락 반대, 잘하길 바랐음
❌ ③ fast: 속도가 아닌 정확성이 핵심
❌ ④ slowly: 속도가 아닌 정확성이 핵심
det.tip: do it right = 올바르게 하다. CPR을 제대로 수행하고 있기를 바라는 마음.

questions.passage: Every night, I had flashbacks of my injury. I could not watch sports anymore because it was just too painful. So I shut out everything related to sports from my life. Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my ordinary high school life without sports. Then one day, I came across an interesting university major called __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 스포츠 의학(sports medicine)이라는 흥미로운 대학 전공을 발견했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ sports medicine: 원문 일치 — 부상의 치료와 예방을 다루는 전공
❌ ① physical therapy: 물리치료, 유사하나 원문 불일치
❌ ② sports journalism: 스포츠 저널리즘, 문맥 부적절
❌ ④ athletic training: 운동 훈련, 문맥 부적절
det.tip: sports medicine(스포츠 의학) — treatment and prevention of sports injuries를 다루는 전공.

questions.passage: This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears. So I made up my mind and applied to this major. Today, thanks to my brave decision, I am studying to be a star on the sidelines instead of on the playing field. __________
questions.stem: 위 글에서 Olivia가 'a star on the sidelines'가 되겠다고 한 것은 무엇을 의미하는가?
ch: 경기장이 아닌 곁에서 선수들을 돕는 전문가가 되겠다.

det.korean: 경기장(playing field)이 아닌 사이드라인(sidelines)에서의 스타 = 스포츠 의학 전문가.
det.analysis:
✅ ② sidelines = 경기장 옆, 스포츠 의학으로 선수를 돕는 전문가
❌ ① 단순 관람자가 아닌 전문가를 의미
❌ ③ playing field가 아닌 sidelines — 선수 복귀가 아님
❌ ④ 해설자는 본문에 언급 없음
det.tip: on the sidelines(사이드라인에서) ↔ on the playing field(경기장에서). 선수→의료 전문가로의 전환.

questions.passage: No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was working in the back. The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk __________ on the floor.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 지각동사 saw + 목적어 + 현재분사. 점원이 바닥에 누워 있는 것을 보았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ lying: 지각동사 saw + 목적어(the clerk) + 현재분사(lying) — 진행 상태
❌ ① lie: 동사원형 가능하나, lying이 진행 상태를 강조하여 더 적절
❌ ② laid: lay(놓다)의 과거형, lie(눕다)와 혼동 주의
❌ ④ to lie: 지각동사 뒤에 to부정사 불가
det.tip: 지각동사(see/hear/feel) + 목적어 + 현재분사(-ing): 진행 중인 동작. lie-lay-lain(눕다) ≠ lay-laid-laid(놓다)

questions.passage: I was about to take the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried off the track. At first, I didn't think much of the injury. I thought I __________ get better soon.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 과거 시점에서의 미래 추측. '나아질 것이라고 생각했다'의 시제 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ② would: 과거 시제(thought)의 간접화법에서 will → would
❌ ① will: 현재 시점의 미래, 시제 불일치
❌ ③ shall: 격식체, 간접화법에 부적절
❌ ④ can: 능력/가능, 맥락 부적절
det.tip: 시제 일치: 주절이 과거(thought)이면 종속절의 will → would. 과거에서 본 미래.

questions.passage: My room was full of medals and awards from races I had competed in. The doctors said my knee injury would prevent me __________ running again.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: prevent A from B: A가 B하는 것을 막다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① from: prevent + 목적어 + from + 동명사 구문
❌ ② to: prevent와 함께 쓰지 않음
❌ ③ for: prevent와 함께 쓰지 않음
❌ ④ of: prevent와 함께 쓰지 않음
det.tip: prevent A from B(~ing): A가 B하는 것을 막다. stop/keep A from ~ing과 동일 패턴.

questions.passage: Ever since I was young, I have admired great public speakers. I hoped __________ and move audiences like them someday. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would get scared.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: hope + to부정사: 영감을 주고 감동시키기를 바랐다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ to inspire: hope + to부정사 구문
❌ ① inspiring: 동명사, hope 뒤에 부적절
❌ ② inspired: 과거분사, hope 뒤에 부적절
❌ ③ inspire: 동사원형, hope 뒤에 to 필요
det.tip: hope + to부정사: hoped to inspire and move. hope는 to부정사만 취한다(동명사 X).

questions.passage: I was scared, but I remembered learning CPR at school. ( ① ) I started to push down on his chest, hoping that I was doing it right. ( ② ) A few minutes later, the paramedics rushed in and took over the situation. ( ③) Luckily, the clerk regained consciousness. ( ④ ) It felt great to help save someone's life!
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"After putting the clerk in the ambulance, the paramedics said 'Thank you for being brave. You did a wonderful job.'"

det.korean: 점원이 의식을 되찾은 후 → 구급차에 태운 뒤 감사 인사 → 생명 구하는 느낌.
det.analysis:
✅ ④: 의식 회복(③ 뒤) → 구급차 이송 + 감사 인사 → 생명 구한 보람(뒤)
❌ ①: CPR 시작 전에 감사 인사는 시간순 위반
❌ ②: 구급대원 도착 전에 감사 인사 불가
❌ ③: 의식 회복 언급 전에 구급차 이송은 부자연스러움
det.tip: 시간순: CPR → 구급대원 도착 → 의식 회복 → 구급차 이송 + 감사 → 보람.

questions.passage: Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my ordinary high school life without sports. ( ① ) Then one day, I came across an interesting university major called sports medicine. ( ② ) It deals with the treatment and prevention of sports injuries. ( ③ ) This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears. ( ④ ) So I made up my mind and applied to this major.
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"A light bulb went on in my head."

det.korean: 스포츠 의학의 내용을 알게 된 후 → 머리에 전구가 켜짐(아이디어) → 문제 도피를 멈출 기회.
det.analysis:
✅ ③: 스포츠 의학 설명(②) 후 영감을 얻음 → 이것이 기회(④ 앞)
❌ ①: 전공 발견 전에 영감을 얻을 수 없음
❌ ②: 전공 내용 설명 전에 영감 불가
❌ ④: 결심 직전보다 기회 인식 전이 더 적절
det.tip: A light bulb went on = 아이디어가 떠오르다. 스포츠 의학의 내용을 알고 나서 깨달음.

questions.passage: Last year, however, was my final chance before graduating from high school. When I saw the poster on the class board, my mind began to fill with thoughts of the school speech contest. I heard a voice growing louder in my head, ①<u>saying</u> "Go for it!" I decided to sign up ②<u>to</u> the contest. To make a long story ③<u>short</u>, I did it. I delivered my speech to the ④<u>entire</u> school.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.korean: ② sign up for(~에 등록하다): to가 아니라 for가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② to → for: sign up for(~에 등록하다). sign up to는 부적절
❌ ① saying: 분사구문, 올바름
❌ ③ short: make a long story short(간단히 말하면), 관용구
❌ ④ entire: 전체의, 형용사로 school 수식
det.tip: sign up for ~: ~에 등록하다/신청하다. sign up to는 '~에 동의하다'로 다른 의미.

questions.passage: So I shut out everything ①<u>related</u> to sports from my life. Two years passed and I was still trying to get ②<u>used to</u> my ordinary high school life without sports. Then one day, I came ③<u>along</u> an interesting university major ④<u>called</u> sports medicine.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.korean: ③ came along → came across: '우연히 발견하다'는 come across이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ along → across: come across(우연히 발견하다). come along(함께 가다/진행되다)은 다른 의미
❌ ① related: 과거분사, everything을 수식, 올바름
❌ ② used to: get used to(~에 익숙해지다), 올바름
❌ ④ called: 과거분사, major를 수식, 올바름
det.tip: come across = 우연히 발견하다. come along = 함께 가다/진행되다. 숙어 전치사 구별!

questions.passage: I went to a convenience store to buy some snacks. No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was working in the back. The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor. I immediately called 911 and explained the situation. The operator asked me to perform CPR on the clerk until the paramedics arrived. I was scared, but I remembered learning CPR at school. I started to push down on his chest, hoping that I was doing it right.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 his가 가리키는 대상은?

det.korean: his = 점원(the clerk). Jason이 점원의 가슴을 눌러 CPR을 수행했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② the clerk: Jason이 CPR을 수행한 대상은 바닥에 쓰러진 점원
❌ ① Jason: 화자(I) 본인, his로 지칭하지 않음
❌ ③ the operator: 전화 교환원, 현장에 없음
❌ ④ the paramedic: 아직 도착하지 않은 상태
det.tip: 대명사 추적: I(Jason)가 push down on his(the clerk's) chest — CPR 대상은 점원.

questions.passage: Then one day, I came across an interesting university major called sports medicine. It deals with the treatment and prevention of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head. This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 This가 가리키는 것은?

det.korean: This = 스포츠 의학이라는 전공을 발견한 것. 문제와 두려움에서 도망치지 않을 기회.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 스포츠 의학을 발견한 것이 도피를 멈출 기회
❌ ① 올림픽은 이미 포기한 꿈
❌ ② 치료가 아닌 전공 선택이 핵심
❌ ③ 차단한 생활은 도피의 일부이지 기회가 아님
det.tip: This(이것) = 바로 앞 문장의 핵심 내용. 스포츠 의학 전공 발견이 전환점.

questions.passage: What does it mean to be brave? There is no single definition, but everyone is brave in their own way. Here are three young people sharing their bravest moments in life.
questions.stem: 세 사람의 이야기를 통해 글 전체가 전달하고자 하는 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 용기는 다양한 형태로 나타나며, 누구나 자기만의 방식으로 용감할 수 있다.
위기 상황에서 응급처치 기술을 배우는 것이 중요하다.
스포츠 부상을 극복하려면 의학적 도움이 필요하다.
대중 앞에서 연설하는 것은 누구에게나 어렵다.

det.korean: 용기는 하나의 정의가 없고, 각자의 방식으로 용감하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 글의 도입부 주제 + 세 사람의 다양한 용기 사례를 통합
❌ ② Jason의 이야기만 해당
❌ ③ Olivia의 이야기만 해당
❌ ④ Yuna의 이야기만 해당
det.tip: 글 전체 주제는 도입부에 제시: no single definition + brave in their own way.

questions.passage: I could not watch sports anymore because it was just too painful. So I shut out everything related to sports from my life. Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my __________ high school life without sports.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 단어 한 개를 원문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: 스포츠 없는 평범한(ordinary) 고등학교 생활에 적응하려 했다.
det.analysis:
